# How to use this edition

This is a retained authoring draft, not validated reviewer or exam coverage.
Follow the matching route; do not run every module. The working steps come
first, with all detailed explanations in the later appendix.

## Default box route

| When                                                  | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                   | Next choice                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Assigned target, no access                            | **NET-01**: ping the assigned IP. No reply does not stop the scan.                                                                                                                         | **NET-02**: one full TCP service scan. A useful result goes to **NET-05**; use **NET-03** only for a specific unresolved service identity and **NET-04** for a justified UDP question.                                   |
| Discovery recorded                                    | **NET-05**: identify and prioritize actual services, not port labels alone.                                                                                                                | Open **one matching service branch** below.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Permitted SSH account or key for an observed endpoint | **SSH-01 → SSH-02**: verify the host key before login, then verify the assigned host and effective identity inside the session.                                                            | A verified Linux shell goes to **LNX-01**; a verified Windows shell goes to **WIN-01**. Denied or unverified access returns to the observed-service route.                                                               |
| Verified Linux shell                                  | **LNX-01 → LNX-03**: keep the host and effective identity, then check only the delegated commands that can change the next action.                                                         | Skip namespace diagnostics unless root, restriction or container evidence makes them relevant. Continue to the exact permission or application lead, then reassess or capture proof.                                     |
| A concrete lead is found                              | Continue the matching service branch: read the relevant file, inspect the application or authenticate with permitted credentials. Use **EXP-01** only when selecting an exploit candidate. | A resulting session goes to **EXP-03** unless the service branch already verified host and identity. A domain credential or graph right opens **AD-09** or **ADCS-01** instead. A domain credential or graph right opens **AD-09** or **ADCS-01** instead. Failed or exhausted leads go to another observed lead or record the specific missing fact before changing branches. |
| Usable session verified                               | **LNX-01** or **WIN-01** according to the actual host; **AD-01** when domain context is assigned or observed.                                                                              | Follow only the permission, identity or objective leads the host provides.                                                                                                                                               |
| Objective reached or route exhausted                  | Use the source step's exact objective proof and cleanup instructions.                                                                                                                      | Keep the output tied to host and identity; record any unresolved cleanup or next question. Do not infer completion from a tool success line.                                                                             |

This is the default _order of decisions_, not a fixed command sequence or a
requirement to enumerate every possible service. A branch opens only when the
assigned target or an actual result supplies its prerequisite and its answer
changes the next action. Otherwise skip it. Start directly at the observed
context when entering with supplied credentials or an existing session.

A readable share file is not an exploit candidate. A permitted SSH login does
not require exploit-source review. A verified session goes directly to host work.
Reuse host and identity output from that same still-open shell rather than
running it again at LNX-01; its full block remains available for direct entry
or a changed shell. Do not repeat EXP-03 merely because the overview mentions
it. Preserve any
cleanup owed by the service or access method you actually used.
An FTP/SMB file that names an exact account for already observed SSH can lead to
SSH-01 only when that one login is permitted. A credential-looking file alone is
not authorization to test it.

For an ordinary verified non-root Linux shell, **LNX-01 → LNX-03** is the short
start. If the exercise supplies an exact user-level objective file for this
identity, check it first in **LNX-01**, then return to LNX-03 if host
work continues. Open LNX-02 only for root/restriction/container context. With
no sudo lead or concrete path, continue at LNX-05 rather than filling a path
template blindly.

In a Quest, open the current task card and expand **What happens next** to see
where each outcome leads. Record the outcome supported by the current context.
Use **Show prior target history** to inspect earlier target records when available.

# Master working checklist 2026-11-21.working.132

Authoring edition; manual decisions are not runtime reviewer coverage.

Sources SHA-256: `ecec4118a4af2cf2dc8f29b82712febe898620d82e82079be85ef91df4a5a731`

# network


Run from Kali. Replace `<TARGET_IP>` with the assigned box.

## NET-01. Check connectivity

Enter when: you have a fresh assigned target.

```bash
ping -c 3 '<TARGET_IP>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| One or more replies from the assigned IP | **NET-02**. |
| No replies | **NET-02**. ICMP silence does not rule out TCP services. |
| Local unreachable-route error | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. Fix the VPN or assigned IP before scanning. |

## NET-02. Scan the box's TCP ports and services

Enter when: the box responds, or you have decided to scan anyway.

```bash
sudo nmap -sS -sVC -p- -v -T4 --open -oA results '<TARGET_IP>'
```

If sudo is unavailable, use `nmap -sT -sVC -p- -v -T4 --open -oA results '<TARGET_IP>'`. If discovery wrongly reports the host down, retry once with `-Pn`. `-oA results` keeps normal, grepable and XML output.

Optionally search the completed XML version scan for local Exploit-DB candidates:

```bash
searchsploit --nmap results.xml
```

`searchsploit --nmap` is a convenience search. It can miss correlations between a service, OS build and advisory. A match is a lead, not proof; check the exact product, version, target OS, architecture, access requirements and side effects in **EXP-01**. No match does not close the service-specific branch.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Completed scan with open ports and versions | **NET-05**. |
| SearchSploit returns a plausible candidate | Keep one product-bearing service; **EXP-01**. |
| Completed scan, no open ports | **NET-04** for a justified UDP question, otherwise **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Stopped at host discovery | Fix the route, then the one `-Pn` retry above. |
| Interrupted or incomplete | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. Keep the partial output. |

## NET-03. Clarify one ambiguous TCP service only if needed

Enter when: one open port's service identity is genuinely unclear.

```bash
nmap -sV -p '<PORT>' '<TARGET_IP>'
```

Add `-Pn` only if discovery gets in the way. Use the protocol's own reply when you can; a version guess is a lead, not a vulnerability.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Service identified or a candidate version returned | **NET-05**. |
| Still ambiguous | One native-protocol probe, otherwise **GAP-SERVICE**. |

## NET-04. Check UDP when a specific question calls for it

Enter when: a TCP clue justifies UDP, e.g. a `smux` or `rpcbind` listener.

```bash
sudo nmap -sU -p 1-1024 -v -oN results.txt '<TARGET_IP>'
```

This covers the top 1024 ports, not all UDP. `open|filtered` is unresolved, not open.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Attributed response | **NET-05** for the matching protocol check. |
| `open\|filtered` or silence | **NET-05** for another lead, or **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Interrupted or failed | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## NET-05 Choose a service to investigate

Enter when: the scan produced at least one service.

Question: Which service should I take next?

Pick one service with a real lead and open its task. An unidentified service returns to NET-03; a service with no task remains a coverage gap. A product-bearing service may open one service-only EXP-01 review.

- http_reported: Nmap reported an HTTP/HTTPS label. WEB-01 must verify the response. Next: WEB-01.
- domain_services_reported: A domain-service label was reported. AD-01 must verify domain and controller context. Next: AD-01.
- ftp_reported: FTP was reported. FTP-01 verifies the protocol and access. Next: FTP-01.
- smb_reported: SMB was reported. SMB-01 verifies shares and identity. Next: SMB-01.
- ssh_reported: SSH was reported. SSH-01 checks host trust and account availability. Next: SSH-01.
- redis_reported: Redis was reported. REDIS-01 proves the connection. Next: REDIS-01.
- dns_reported: DNS was reported. DNS-01 asks the resolver. Next: DNS-01.
- rpc_nfs_reported: RPC/NFS was reported. NFS-01 checks the export. Next: NFS-01.
- snmp_reported: SNMP was reported. SNMP-01 tests one community. Next: SNMP-01.
- database_reported: A database was reported. DB-01 confirms the engine and login. Next: DB-01.
- mail_reported: A mail protocol was reported. MAIL-01 confirms protocol and TLS. Next: MAIL-01.
- smtp_reported: SMTP was reported. SMTP-01 checks users and relay. Next: SMTP-01.
- docker_reported: A Docker API was reported. DOCKER-01 tests it unauthenticated. Next: DOCKER-01.
- jenkins_reported: Jenkins was reported. JENKINS-01 checks the script console. Next: JENKINS-01.
- tftp_reported: TFTP was reported. TFTP-01 tests one filename. Next: TFTP-01.
- rsync_reported: Rsync was reported. RSYNC-01 lists modules. Next: RSYNC-01.
- ipmi_reported: IPMI was reported. IPMI-01 checks the BMC. Next: IPMI-01.
- vnc_reported: VNC was reported. VNC-01 checks the desktop. Next: VNC-01.
- ntp_reported: NTP was reported. NTP-01 checks the server. Next: NTP-01.
- x11_reported: X11 was reported. X11-01 checks display access. Next: X11-01.
- squid_reported: A proxy was reported. SQUID-01 tests it. Next: SQUID-01.
- unfamiliar_service: No specific task fits. Follow GENERIC-01. Next: GENERIC-01.
- rdp_reported: RDP was reported. RDP-01 checks the permitted account. Next: RDP-01.
- product_bearing_service_selected: A non-web service carries a scanner-qualified product. One candidate review is justified. Next: EXP-01.
- other_service: No task matches the service. Keep a specific gap. Next: GAP-SERVICE.
- no_justified_lead: No service has a lead. Keep a resumable pause. Next: PAUSE-COVERAGE.

# ftp

One authorized write test on an observed FTP path.

Verified FTPS or STARTTLS listing on one endpoint.

## FTP-01. List under the exact permitted identity

Enter when: an FTP service answered.

```bash
curl -sS 'ftp://<TARGET_IP>:<FTP_PORT>/'
```

For a supplied account on plain FTP, curl prompts for the password:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff -sS --connect-timeout 5 --ftp-pasv --ftp-skip-pasv-ip --user '<USERNAME>' 'ftp://<TARGET_IP>:<FTP_PORT>/'
```

If the server requires TLS, use **FTP-04** instead.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Listing returned | **FTP-02**. A listing is not file access. |
| Login denied | **PASS-03** against `ftp://`, or **NET-05** when no username is suspected. |
| Login works, listing or data channel fails | Check the route at **NET-01**, then **NET-05**. |
| Writable directory and write test permitted | **FTP-03**. |
| TLS required | **FTP-04**. |

## FTP-02 Check one relevant FTP file

Enter when: FTP-01 returned a listing as your identity.

```bash
curl --disable --globoff --path-as-is -sS --fail --connect-timeout 5 --max-filesize 1048576 --ftp-pasv --ftp-skip-pasv-ip --user 'anonymous:' --output './<LOCAL_COPY>.bin' 'ftp://<TARGET_IP>:<FTP_PORT>/<LISTED_PATH>'
```

Use your supplied username in place of `anonymous:`. For FTPS, copy the matching verified command from FTP-04.

```bash
sha256sum -- './<LOCAL_COPY>.bin'; file -- './<LOCAL_COPY>.bin'
sed -n '1,80p' './<LOCAL_COPY>.bin' | cat -v
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Transfer completed | Inspect the copy. ZIP or key material goes to **ART-01**; an account for observed SSH goes to **SSH-01**; otherwise **NET-05**. |
| Login denied | **FTP-01**, or **FTP-04** for the FTPS context. |
| Access denied or file missing | Keep the path and response; **NET-05**. |
| Data-channel or TLS failure | **NET-01** / **FTP-04**. A partial file is not a read. |

Delete the copy once it is triaged: `rm -i -- './<LOCAL_COPY>.bin'`.

## FTP-03. Does one observed FTP write path accept and remove an inert file?

```bash
printf 'probe\n' | curl --disable --globoff -sS --fail --user '<USERNAME>' --upload-file - 'ftp://<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>/<DIR>/probe-<ID>.txt'
curl --disable --globoff -sS --fail --user '<USERNAME>' -o probe.copy 'ftp://<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>/<DIR>/probe-<ID>.txt'
curl --disable --globoff --list-only -sS --fail --user '<USERNAME>' --quote '+DELE probe-<ID>.txt' 'ftp://<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>/<DIR>/'
rm probe.copy
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Upload, read and delete succeed | **NET-05**; not execution. |
| Write denied | **FTP-01** / **NET-05**. |
| Upload ok, read fails | Attempt cleanup, otherwise **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |
| Delete denied or file remains | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## FTP-04. Does the observed FTP TLS endpoint give a verified listing?

Implicit FTPS:

```bash
curl --disable --globoff --path-as-is -sS --fail --ftp-pasv --cacert '<CA>' --resolve '<CERT_HOST>:<PORT>:<TARGET_IP>' --user '<USERNAME>' -w 'TLS %{ssl_verify_result}\n' 'ftps://<CERT_HOST>:<PORT>/<DIR>/'
```

For STARTTLS use `--ssl-reqd` and `ftp://`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Verified TLS and listing | **FTP-02** in this TLS context. |
| Certificate failure | **PAUSE-ROUTE**; do not use `-k`. |
| TLS fails before auth | **NET-03**. |
| Login denied | **NET-05**. |

# smb

One authorized write test on an observed SMB path.

## SMB-01 List shares for the current identity

Enter when: SMB answered.

Record the protocol, dialect, OS and signing evidence before choosing a branch:

```bash
sudo nmap -Pn -n -p445 --script smb-protocols,smb2-capabilities,smb2-security-mode,smb-os-discovery '<TARGET_IP>'
```

```text
smbclient -N -L '//<TARGET_IP>'
```

For a supplied account, use `-U '<DOMAIN_OR_SERVER>\<USERNAME>'` and let smbclient prompt:

```bash
smbclient -L '<TARGET_IP>' -p '<SMB_PORT>' -U '<DOMAIN_OR_SERVER>\<USERNAME>' --timeout 15
```

An OS, service pack or SMB dialect match is only a vulnerability candidate. For example, Windows Server 2008 SP1 with SMB 2.0.2 does not prove CVE-2009-3103. Correlate the observed OS/build, SMB generation and service evidence with local source, then map its affected-version claims to a vendor advisory and CVE. Search installed checks only after that mapping:

```bash
searchsploit --disable-colour '<OBSERVED_OS_OR_SERVICE>' '<OBSERVED_VERSION_OR_SMB_DIALECT>'
searchsploit -x <EDB_ID>
find /usr/share/nmap/scripts -maxdepth 1 -type f -iname 'smb-vuln*.nse' -printf '%f\n'
```

Use **MSF-01** to search installed Metasploit modules by the mapped CVE or product. Treat source comments and module names as leads until the advisory's exact affected releases and conditions match.

Before any SMB vulnerability script, inspect `nmap --script-help '<SCRIPT>'` and note `intrusive`, `exploit` or `dos` categories. Run a destructive check only with explicit authorization and a working reset or recovery path. Run it once, then check the specific service rather than repeating the vulnerability probe:

```bash
nmap --script-help '<SMB_VULN_SCRIPT>'
sudo nmap -Pn -n -p445 --script '<SMB_VULN_SCRIPT>' --script-timeout 180s '<TARGET_IP>'
nmap -Pn -n -sV -p445 '<TARGET_IP>'
```

Some SMB checks, including the CVE-2009-3103 check, are intrusive and DoS-capable. A vulnerable host may crash or reset. If the host or TCP 445 is unstable, recover or reset the lab and do not repeat the check.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Shares listed | **SMB-02**. A share name is not read access. |
| Login or share-list denied | **NET-05**. |
| Domain or controller clue | **AD-01**. |
| Candidate version or dialect only | Not proof. Run an authorized dedicated check or keep the hypothesis in **EXP-01**. |
| Dedicated script reports `VULNERABLE` | Save the output; **EXP-01**, or **MSF-01** if using the allowance. |
| Host crashes, resets or drops SMB | Stop retries; recover the target, then **PAUSE-RECOVERY** until SMB is stable. |
| Transport or identity error | **NET-03**. |

## SMB-02 Read a relevant SMB share path

Enter when: you have a listed share and a known identity.

```bash
smbclient '//<TARGET_IP>/<SHARE>' -I '<TARGET_IP>' -p '<SMB_PORT>' -U '<DOMAIN_OR_SERVER>\<USERNAME>' --timeout 15
```

At the `smb: \>` prompt, list, then fetch one file and quit:

```text
ls
cd "<DIRECTORY>"
get "<FILE>" "./<LOCAL_COPY>.bin"
quit
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| File transferred | Inspect the copy as in FTP-02. ZIP or key material goes to **ART-01**; account-plus-SSH goes to **SSH-01**; otherwise **NET-05**. |
| Share denied or logon denied | **SMB-01**. |
| Path or file denied | Keep the path; **NET-05**. |
| Share writable and write test permitted | **SMB-03**. |
| Timeout or partial copy | Not a completed read; retry or **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## SMB-03. Does one observed SMB write path accept and remove an inert file?

Enter when: SMB-02 read access works and write access is the question.

```bash
smbclient '//<TARGET_IP>/<SHARE>' -I '<TARGET_IP>' -p '<SMB_PORT>' -U '<DOMAIN_OR_SERVER>\<USERNAME>' --timeout 15
```

At the prompt, create, list, delete:

```text
ls
put /etc/hostname "probe-<RUN_ID>.txt"
ls "probe-<RUN_ID>.txt"
del "probe-<RUN_ID>.txt"
quit
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Write, read-back and delete all succeed | Record the writable path; **NET-05** or the application that consumes it. |
| Write denied | **NET-05**. Read access did not imply write. |
| Write succeeds, delete fails | Keep the path and go to **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |
| Transport or identity error | **SMB-01**. |

# remote_access

## SSH-01 Check the observed SSH access boundary

Enter when: SSH answered.

```text
ssh-keyscan -T 5 -p <SSH_PORT> <TARGET_IP>
```

Compare the host key with anything already pinned. If one account is supplied, go straight to **SSH-02**; with no account, **PASS-03** is the guess route. Do not spray when a working supplied account exists.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoint answers, key unchanged, account supplied | **SSH-02**. |
| Endpoint answers, no account | **PASS-03** against `ssh://`; SSH stays a blocked prerequisite. |
| Pinned key changed | **PAUSE-ROUTE** until explained. |
| Port closed but a knock sequence was read | **SSH-03**. |
| Connection fails before key exchange | **NET-03**. |

## SSH-02. Verify one permitted SSH session and enter its host branch

Enter when: SSH-01 confirmed the endpoint and you have a permitted credential.

```bash
ssh -p '<SSH_PORT>' '<USERNAME>@<TARGET_IP>'
```

Use `-i '<KEY_PATH>' -o IdentitiesOnly=yes` instead when a key was supplied. Inside the session:

```bash
hostname; id; uname -s
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Linux host and identity confirmed | **LNX-01** in this shell. |
| Windows host and identity confirmed | **WIN-01** in this shell. |
| Login denied | **PASS-03** against `ssh://` with that name, or **NET-05** when no username is suspected. |
| Logged in but host or identity unverified | **EXP-03**. |

## SSH-03. Use an observed opening sequence, then close that access

Enter when a read at WREAD-01 or LNX-07 supplied the host's actual knock sequence and you may change its firewall.

Record both event blocks: ordered ports and protocols, `seq_timeout`, flags, action and the opening/closing pair for the exact SSH port. Unknown flags or one-time sequences go to **PAUSE-COVERAGE**.

Check the baseline from the same client:

```bash
ip route get '<TARGET_IP>'
nmap -n -Pn -sT -p '<SSH_PORT>' --max-retries 1 --host-timeout 15s '<TARGET_IP>'
```

If already open, go to **SSH-01** without knocking. Otherwise send the opening sequence once:

```bash
knock -4 -v -d '<DELAY_MS>' '<TARGET_IP>' '<PORT1>:tcp' '<PORT2>:tcp' '<PORT3>:tcp'
nmap -n -Pn -sT -p '<SSH_PORT>' --max-retries 1 --host-timeout 15s '<TARGET_IP>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Port opens | **SSH-01**, then **SSH-02**. |
| Still closed or scan incomplete | Send the closing sequence once, then **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Route changed | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

After SSH work, exit your shells, recheck the route and send the actual closing sequence once. Verify the port is filtered again.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Port returns to the closed baseline | Continue the workflow. |
| Port open or baseline unconfirmed | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

# http


Work one origin at a time: scheme, hostname, port.

## WEB-01. Initial web triage

Enter when: an endpoint answers HTTP.

Open the exact URL, browse the visible functions, and read source and Network requests. For a blank or broken render, inspect the failed request. For a plain read-only GET you can repeat safely:

```bash
curl -i '<EXACT_URL>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Paths, forms or functions found | **[WEB-04](./web-04)**, **[WEB-06](./web-06)**, **[WEB-08](./web-08)**. |
| Redirect or link to another hostname | **WEB-05**. |
| Login or 401/403 | **WEB-09**. |
| 404 or soft-404 | **WEB-04** with the missing-path baseline. |
| Repeated 5xx, 429 or broken transport | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

GET and request work continues at **WEB-06** and **WEB-08**. Advanced paths: **WEB-13**, **WEB-14**, **WEB-15**, **WEB-16**, **WEB-17**, **WEB-18**, **WEB-19**, **WEB-20**, **WEB-21**, **WEB-22**, **WEB-23**.

## WEB-04 Discover unlinked directories and files

Enter when: you have a working base URL.

Pick one scanner; gobuster is the lighter default.

```bash
gobuster dir -u '<TARGET_URL>/' -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirbuster/directory-list-2.3-medium.txt -x php,html,txt,bak,old,zip,conf -t 50 -o gobuster.txt
```

Or feroxbuster, which resumes a stopped run and filters wildcard responses:

```bash
feroxbuster -u '<TARGET_URL>/' -w /usr/share/wordlists/dirbuster/directory-list-2.3-medium.txt -x php,html,txt,bak,old,zip,conf -t 50 -o feroxbuster.txt
```

Establish a false-response baseline first and reduce threads on 429.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Dynamic path or input | **WEB-03**, **WEB-06** or **WEB-08**. |
| Input implied but its name is unknown | **WEB-07**. |
| Downloaded file | **ART-01**. |
| Wildcard or filtering noise | Compare against the baseline, then one retry. |
| Nothing new | **NET-05**. |
| Rate limited or unstable | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## WEB-03 Fingerprint the application

Enter when: a page or a nested app responds.

```bash
whatweb -a 1 -v --follow-redirect=never '<TARGET_URL>'
```

A scanner string is a hint, not a confirmed version.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Product confirmed by the response | **EXP-01** with that version. |
| CMS named | **WEB-11**. |
| Observed GET or form input | **WEB-06** / **WEB-08**. |
| WebDAV or default-file lead | **WEB-12**. |
| Product stays unconfirmed | **WEB-01**. |

## WEB-06 Inspect and replay an observed GET parameter

Enter when: a real GET request and its normal value are captured.

```bash
curl -sS -i --get '<TARGET_URL>' --data-urlencode '<FIELD>=<BENIGN_VALUE>'
```

Compare status, body and redirect with the normal value.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing changes | **NET-05**. |
| Input-dependent error or anomaly | **GAP-WEB-INPUT**. |
| Value names a file | **WREAD-01**. |
| Value reaches a POSIX shell argument | **WEXEC-01**. |
| Numeric value feeds a query | **WSQL-01**. |

## WEB-08 Inspect a form or API request

Enter when: a real form or API request is captured.

```bash
curl -sS -i --request POST '<TARGET_URL>' \
  --data-urlencode '<FIELD>=<BENIGN_VALUE>' \
  --data-urlencode '<REQUIRED_FIELD>=<CAPTURED_VALUE>'
```

Keep the captured method, content type and every required field. JSON or multipart goes through Burp or the browser.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Nothing changes | **NET-05**, or **WEB-04** if discovery is unfinished. |
| Upload function observed | **WEB-10**. |
| Stored create/update with a delete route | **WSTORE-01**. |
| Required account observed | **WEB-09**; a login form goes to **PASS-04**. |
| POSIX argument, file read or SQL context | **WEXEC-01** / **WREAD-01** / **WSQL-01**. |
| Anomaly | **GAP-WEB-INPUT**. |
| JSON body | **WEB-26**. |
| GraphQL or OAuth | **WEB-27**. |

## WEB-05. Check one observed hostname

Enter when: a redirect or link names an in-scope hostname.

```bash
curl -i --resolve '<HOSTNAME>:<PORT>:<TARGET_IP>' '<EXACT_URL>'
```

Use the same scheme, hostname and port in both the URL and `--resolve`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Distinct in-scope app | **WEB-01** at that origin. |
| Same content or false-host response | **WEB-04**. |
| Scope unclear | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |
| TLS or transport error | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## WEB-07 Discover missing GET parameter names

Enter when: a page implies an input whose name is not in the HTML or scripts.

```bash
ffuf -u '<TARGET_URL>?FUZZ=test' -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/burp-parameter-names.txt -mc all -t 10 -rate 20 -maxtime 120
```

Or measure the response to an unknown parameter and filter that exact byte size:

```bash
curl -sS '<TARGET_URL>?unlikely_parameter_name=test' | wc -c
ffuf -u '<TARGET_URL>?FUZZ=test' -w /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/Web-Content/burp-parameter-names.txt -mc all -fs '<BASELINE_BYTES>' -t 10 -rate 20 -maxtime 120
```

Compare against an unknown parameter; confirm a hit through **WEB-06**.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Distinct candidate | **WEB-06**. |
| Nothing distinct | **WEB-01**. |

## WEB-09. Check a signed-in function

Enter when: a function needs a permitted account.

Sign in through the UI, confirm the account and origin, then open one account-only function and inspect its request. Do not forward cookies to another origin.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Account-only function works | **WEB-06**, **WEB-08** or **WEB-10**. |
| No permitted account | **PASS-04** on the observed login form, then **WEB-01**. |
| Login redirect or expired session | Resolve sign-in first. |
| Identity confirmed but function denied | Record the boundary; **WEB-01**. |

Enter when: an upload form is on screen.

Read the request in Network: file field, accepted type, required fields, returned path and delete action.

| Result | Next |

| Extension or content-type gate | **WUPLOAD-03**. |
| Existing template is edited, not uploaded | **WEDIT-01**. |
| Identity or fields unclear | **WEB-09** / **WEB-08**. |

## WEB-28. Enumerate one confirmed WordPress installation with WPScan

Enter when the response confirms WordPress through `/wp-content/`, `/wp-admin/`, `/wp-login.php`, `/wp-json/` or equivalent page source. Use the exact installation root without a trailing slash, including a subdirectory when WordPress is not at `/`.

If the IP redirects to an in-scope hostname, add that exact mapping to `/etc/hosts`, then scan the hostname rather than the IP:

```text
sudoedit /etc/hosts
<TARGET_IP>    <WORDPRESS_HOSTNAME>
```

Update a stale local database. Load the API token without putting it in shell history; WPScan reads `WPSCAN_API_TOKEN` automatically. The token adds vulnerability data, but enumeration still works without it.

```bash
wpscan --update
read -rsp 'WPScan API token: ' WPSCAN_API_TOKEN; export WPSCAN_API_TOKEN; printf '\n'
wpscan --url '<WORDPRESS_ROOT>' \
  --enumerate ap,at,u,cb,dbe \
  --detection-mode aggressive \
  --plugins-detection aggressive \
  --plugins-version-detection aggressive \
  --output wpscan.txt \
  --format cli-no-colour \
  --verbose
```

The combined scan is the default. Use a focused retry only when one part is missing or unclear:

```bash
# Users
wpscan --url '<WORDPRESS_ROOT>' --enumerate u --detection-mode aggressive --verbose

# Plugins
wpscan --url '<WORDPRESS_ROOT>' --enumerate ap \
  --plugins-detection aggressive --plugins-version-detection aggressive --verbose

# Themes
wpscan --url '<WORDPRESS_ROOT>' --enumerate at \
  --themes-detection aggressive --themes-version-detection aggressive --verbose
```

For an authorized password test, use only confirmed usernames. Start with the supplied or short box-specific list; use `rockyou.txt` only when the lab permits the larger attempt and the endpoint stays stable.

```bash
wpscan --url '<WORDPRESS_ROOT>' --usernames users.txt --passwords passwords.txt
wpscan --url '<WORDPRESS_ROOT>' \
  --usernames '<CONFIRMED_USERNAME>' \
  --passwords /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
```

Keep `wpscan.txt` with the report. Confidence is scanner evidence, not proof. Confirm the reachable component path and version, then inspect the local source before trying a candidate:

```bash
searchsploit --disable-colour --title 'WordPress <PLUGIN_OR_THEME>' '<VERSION>'
searchsploit -x <EDB_ID>
```

ColdBoxEasy example: Site Editor through 1.1.1 maps to EDB-ID 44340 and CVE-2018-7422. This is a pre-foothold file-read check, not post-exploitation enumeration. Use it only after the plugin and affected version match:

```bash
searchsploit -x 44340
curl -sS -i --get \
  '<WORDPRESS_ROOT>/wp-content/plugins/site-editor/editor/extensions/pagebuilder/includes/ajax_shortcode_pattern.php' \
  --data-urlencode 'ajax_path=/etc/passwd'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Plugin or theme and affected version confirmed | **EXP-01** with the saved local source. |
| Site Editor returns the requested local file | **WREAD-01**. |
| A permitted credential works | **WEB-09**. |
| More WordPress paths appear | **WEB-04**. |
| Only a version hint or low-confidence match appears | **WEB-03**. |
| Scan is rate limited or destabilizes the endpoint | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

```text
curl -sS -i -X OPTIONS '<TARGET_URL>'
curl -sS -i -X PROPFIND -H 'Depth: 0' '<TARGET_URL>'
```

Optional default-file pass: `nikto -h '<TARGET_URL>' -Tuning 2b`. A `DAV` header or 207 is a lead, not access.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| DAV collection with a validated credential | **AD-15**. |
| DAV without credentials | **WEB-09**. |
| Useful default file | **WEB-01**. |
| Nothing confirmed | **NET-05**. |

```

| Identity unclear | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |

```

## WIN-01. Identify this Windows shell

Enter when: you have a new Windows shell or changed token.

```powershell
hostname
whoami
whoami /all
```

Match the hostname to the assigned target and read the actual token, not the username.

If `whoami` returns `nt authority\system` and the objective names a file, collect only that objective:

```powershell
Get-Item -LiteralPath '<OBJECTIVE_PATH>' | Select-Object FullName, Length, LastWriteTimeUtc
certutil.exe -hashfile "<OBJECTIVE_PATH>" SHA256
Get-Content -LiteralPath '<OBJECTIVE_PATH>'
```

Keep the hostname, `whoami /all`, exact path and hash as privilege and objective proof. Do not recurse profiles or collect unrelated credential stores.

| Result | Next |

| Ordinary or restricted token | **WIN-16**, then **WIN-02** or **WIN-03**. |

| Enabled `SeLoadDriverPrivilege` / `SeCreateTokenPrivilege` / `SeTcbPrivilege` | **WPRIV-07** / **WPRIV-08**. |
| Medium integrity while in Administrators | **WPRIV-09**. |
| Loopback listener | **WIN-12**. |
| Host or token unverified | **EXP-03**. |

## WIN-14. Prepare one reviewed Windows candidate without replacement
